answer_1.quote: We build Planorama (Figure ): an interface to log users' success when solving multi-step questions assisted by LLM plans (helpfulness) and selections on plans users think help them (preferences).
answer_1.outputs: step-by-step plans (sequences of high-level steps) for multi-step math and trivia questions

answer_2.quote: We log users' accuracy-if they answer q correctly on their first try-and execution time-how many seconds they take-when using p; we later combine these into a single score to label which plan p ∈ P best helps users ( §5.1)... Macro-average accuracy and time in users who executed LLM plans...

answer_3.quote: We also use GPT-4o as a generative RM , LLM-as-a-judge), predicting which p ∈ P helps users answer q more accurately/quickly-mirroring user pairwise comparisons ( §3.2.1)... We find plans models prefer via judgments from six reward models and GPT-4o ( §4.2)...

answer_4.quote: We have 126 users... collecting 4388 execution traces and 5584 preferences on 600 question/plan pairs... For preferences, we use pairwise comparisons-the standard alignment feedback. In a round of Planorama, users see a new question q and its plans P in a random order, and pick which p ∈ P they think will help them solve q more accurately/quickly... We deploy LLM-created plans in our interface to help users solve multi-step math and trivia questions...
answer_4.guideline: Which plan p ∈ P they think will help them solve q more accurately/quickly
